- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, check for overshoot after spike — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to adjust — apply mean reversion rule: subtract 1–3% from forecast if recent 3–5 days show decline.  
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model may be overconfident — apply conservative correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model is rising steadily and true outcome shows early drop, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in first 5–7 days of forecast window.  
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.20 spikes, model may be overfitting — apply smoothing: average last 3–5 forecast values before applying correction.
